key_insight: World Tracing bridges the gap between accurate depth alignment and full 3D completion by generating geometry that stays anchored to visible pixels while extending beyond what the camera sees. In simple terms, it aims to make image-to-3D outputs both faithful to the input and complete as a shape.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the common trade-off in image-to-3D reconstruction: depth methods align well with visible surfaces but cannot infer hidden geometry, while generative 3D models can complete shapes but often drift away from the observed image.
method: Introduces a generative pixel-aligned geometry representation called World Tracing.
Predicts 3D points for each input pixel using an ordered stack of camera-space geometry along the ray.
Completes occluded or invisible structure beyond the visible surface while preserving alignment with the input image.
impact: This approach could improve image-to-3D systems that need both realism and geometric consistency, making them more useful for AR/VR, robotics, digital asset creation, and scene reconstruction. For practitioners, it offers a stronger representation for reconciling observed evidence with plausible hidden structure.
